title: Review: Largest Number
context: A teammate wrote this for Find Largest Number and asked you to review it before it's merged. You're reviewing their code, not writing your own.

findings.title: The running maximum starts at 0
findings.explanation: largest starts at 0, so a value only replaces it if it is above 0. When every value is negative, none is, and the method returns 0: a number that isn't in the array.
findings.consequence: Any array of only negative numbers gets the wrong answer. Public test 2 shows it: [-5, -2, -11] should give -2 and gets 0.
findings.repair: Start from a real value: int largest = nums[0]; (the empty case is already handled above it). The loop can then start at index 1.

findings.title: An index loop where only the values are used
findings.explanation: The loop uses i only to read nums[i]. for (int n : nums) would say that more directly.
findings.consequence: None for correctness: both loops visit every value once.
findings.repair: Optional: switch to an enhanced for loop if your team prefers it.
findings.why_preference: No input behaves differently either way, so no test can tell the two apart. It's a style choice, not a defect.

debrief: One real defect, shown by a public test: the maximum starts at 0, so all-negative arrays return 0. The empty-array contract is handled correctly. The index loop is a preference; a review that called it a bug would be wrong.
review_status: Written for practice and machine-checked: the code and the repair were run against every test of the problem.
